sections.h2: Where is Rochester, Minnesota, and what should a home seller know about the city?
sections.html:
Rochester is the county seat of Olmsted County in southeast Minnesota, about 85 miles from Minneapolis and Saint Paul. It sits on the south fork of the Zumbro River at the western edge of the Driftless Area, and the Census Bureau counts 56.8 square miles of land inside the city limits.

George Head built a log tavern here in 1854 and named the settlement for his hometown in New York. The Winona and St. Peter Railroad arrived in October 1864, and the 1883 tornado that flattened much of the town led directly to the hospital that grew into Mayo Clinic. Olmsted is one of only four Minnesota counties with no natural lake, so the water you see in town, such as Silver Lake, was made by damming the river.

The Census Bureau estimates 124,292 people lived in Rochester on July 1, 2025, up 2.4 percent from the April 2020 base and well above the 106,769 counted in 2010. That makes it the third largest city in the state. Sellers here are dealing with a city that keeps adding households, which shapes how quickly a well kept house draws attention.

sections.h2: How does the Rochester economy affect the housing market?
sections.html:
Medicine drives it. Mayo Clinic was born in Rochester, and the Census Bureau's 2022 economic data shows health care and social assistance receipts of about $2.98 billion in the city, next to roughly $3.40 billion in retail sales. Workers in those fields, plus the students at the University of Minnesota Rochester and Rochester Community and Technical College, keep a steady stream of renters and first-time buyers in the market.

The state's Destination Medical Center plan, signed in 2013, is meant to channel a multibillion dollar Mayo investment into downtown districts such as Discovery Square and Heart of the City. Construction near the river and the medical campus can change the feel of a nearby block, so a seller close to downtown should expect buyers to ask about it.

Not every owner has time for a retail listing. Typical situations in a university and hospital town include:

  • a relocation after a residency, fellowship or job change;
  • a rental left behind by a tenant who moved out;
  • a house inherited from a relative who lived in another state;
  • an older home with deferred repairs that would be expensive to fix before listing.

sections.h2: What do Rochester winters, wind and storms mean for an older house?
sections.html:
Rochester has a warm-summer humid continental climate and averages about 33 inches of rain and 52 inches of snow a year. Wikipedia lists it as the second windiest city in the country, with winds averaging 12.6 mph, and the January to April stretch is the windiest.

Severe weather has left a record. Two F4 tornadoes hit the city in 1953 and 1962, a June 2010 tornado damaged homes around the Lincolnshire neighborhood on the northwest side, and a June 2019 storm hit southwest Rochester. A 1978 flood led the city to rework nearby rivers and streams for flood control.

  • Roof and siding that have taken years of wind are the first things an inspector looks at.
  • Basements near the Zumbro and its creeks deserve a moisture check before you list or accept an offer.
  • Frozen-pipe damage in a vacant house is a real winter risk, so keep the heat on during a sale.

A buyer paying cash usually takes a storm-worn house as it stands, which spares you the repair bids.

sections.h2: How do roads, transit and schools shape a Rochester sale?
sections.html:
Three U.S. highways cross the city: U.S. 14, U.S. 52 and U.S. 63. Interstate 90 and State Highway 30 skirt the southern edge, and downtown buildings are tied together by skyways and underground walkways that people use to stay out of the cold. Rochester International Airport is seven miles south of downtown, with flights to Atlanta, Chicago, Denver and Minneapolis.

A 2.6 mile bus rapid transit line called Link, planned along 2nd Street Southwest, is listed for an August 2027 opening. Homes within walking distance of that corridor may draw different questions from buyers than homes in the outer ring.

Rochester Public Schools serves the city, with three high school attendance zones: John Marshall, Mayo and Century. Private options include Lourdes and Rochester Central Lutheran School. The attendance zone for a particular address is worth confirming with the district before you quote it in a listing.

sections.h2: What must a Rochester landlord do before selling a rental house?
sections.html:
Anyone renting out a dwelling in Rochester needs a Rental Housing Certificate under city ordinance chapter 7-3-2, including a single-family house the owner does not live in. The city says renting without one is a misdemeanor punishable by up to a $1,000 fine, 90 days in jail, or both.

  • Certificates renew each year, and the fee depends on the number of units.
  • Inspection scores set a one, two, three or four year cycle, and a compliant inspection is required in the year it is due.
  • A certificate must be transferred within 30 days of a property sale, and the city has a termination form for owners who have sold.
  • A building that sits vacant must be registered within 30 days under ordinance 7-14-6, and an annual vacant building fee follows.

Short stays of up to 30 days follow separate rules. A second home listed on a rental platform needs a Short Term Rental license and a compliant inspection, while an owner-occupied room rental needs registration. For questions, the Community Development office is at 4001 W. River Parkway NW, Suite 100, and the city's main line is 507-328-2311.

sections.h2: When are Olmsted County property taxes due, and who pays at closing?
sections.html:
The county's 2026 real estate dates are May 15 for the first half and October 15 for the second half, with agricultural second-half taxes listed for November 16, 2026. Both of the main real estate dates have passed, so the next installment for a house is the first half due in May 2027.

Olmsted County tells new owners that taxes on a mid-year sale are split at closing: the seller covers January through the closing date and the buyer covers the rest of the year. If the seller already paid the full year, the buyer reimburses that share. No statement is mailed to a mid-year purchaser, and the county says not receiving one does not excuse a late payment.

After a sale the county mails the new owner a homestead application. Return it, because the homestead classification determines the value exclusion that lowers the tax bill. Questions go to the county's revenue and records line at 507-328-7636.

sections.h2: How can I appeal my Rochester property value?
sections.html:
Start by collecting recent appraisals or sales of similar houses, then call the Assessor's Office at 507-328-7670 or visit Property Records at 151 4th Street SE. If that does not settle it, use the appeal meetings listed on your valuation notice. When the city has a local board, you begin there, and otherwise you go straight to the county board.

The last step is a petition to the Minnesota Tax Court, filed after the valuation notice arrives and before April 30 of the year the taxes are payable. Olmsted County accepts service of those petitions by email, and a paper copy can be delivered to the County Attorney's Office at 151 Fourth Street Southeast.

The 2026 appeal calendar has closed, so a change to the 2026 value is no longer available to you. The next notices arrive in the spring.

sections.h2: What are the transfer and disclosure steps when a Rochester house sells?
sections.html:
Minnesota charges deed tax of .0033 of the net consideration on a conveyed deed, with a $1.65 minimum when the price is $3,000 or less (Minn. Stat. 287.21). The tax is due when the deed is presented for recording, and your closing agent normally handles it. Ask Olmsted County Property Records and Licensing how the deed should be submitted.

Before you sign a purchase agreement, state law has you hand the buyer a written disclosure of radon test results and any mitigation system, plus the Department of Health publication on radon in real estate (Minn. Stat. 144.496). A transfer to an heir is one of the exceptions.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rochester house without fixing it first?
faqs.a: Yes. Nothing in the Rochester sources requires repairs before a sale between private parties, and an as-is buyer takes the house in its current condition. A landlord still needs the rental certificate and inspection status in order, so check that before you accept an offer on a tenant-occupied house.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell a buyer about radon?
faqs.a: Yes. Minnesota requires a written radon disclosure before you sign an agreement to sell residential property, and a seller who withholds known radon facts can be sued within two years after closing. The disclosure covers any tests, reports and mitigation system you know about.

faqs.q: What happens to my rental certificate when I sell a Rochester rental?
faqs.a: It has to be transferred within 30 days of the sale, and the city offers a termination form for owners who have sold. Contact Community Development at 507-328-2311 so the certificate does not stay in your name.

faqs.q: Who pays property tax on the day a Rochester house closes?
faqs.a: The county says the seller pays from January to the closing date and the buyer pays from closing to December 31. If the seller prepaid the whole year, the buyer repays the seller for the buyer's part at closing.

faqs.q: Is it too late to appeal this year's Rochester assessment?
faqs.a: For the 2026 value, yes, because the county appeal meetings are over. The Minnesota Tax Court route stays open until April 30 of the year the taxes are payable, so the next notice you receive starts a new window.
